- [RCTS.1.2.28] **The session's inputs** — wherever a fixture's `expect`
  carries an array of steps (`steps`, and `clone_determinism`'s `after_clone`
  and `after_free`), each step is an object whose `op` names one member of a
  closed set, and which carries exactly the members that op takes. A harness
  must give the runtime under test each step in order, through the runtime's
  own interface, on the harness's mock clocks:

  - `assert`, with `schema`, a string, and optionally `slots`, an object;
    `as`, a string; `corr_from_call`, a non-negative integer; and `refused`
    ([RCTS.1.2.27]). It is a host assert of a fact of `schema` whose slots
    have `slots`' values. A `Bytes` value is written `{"$bytes": H}`, H its
    octets as two hex digits each, and nothing else. A `String` value may be
    written `{"$text_bytes": H}`, H its text's octets as two hex digits each,
    none of them `00` ([LSTR.1.5]), which need not be well-formed UTF-8: a harness must give the runtime
    those octets as the slot's text, unchanged, which is how a fixture hands
    the engine text [LSTR.8.5] refuses, and must fail a fixture that gives
    the form to a slot of another kind. With `as`, the fact the
    assert answers with is kept under that label. With `corr_from_call` N,
    the `corr` slot takes the correlation the N-th call issued so far
    carried, counting from 0 in the order the calls were issued
    ([LCCO.3.4]); a harness must fail the fixture when fewer than N + 1
    calls have been issued.
  - `retract`, with `label`, a string: a host retract of the fact kept under
    that label. A harness must fail the fixture when no earlier `assert`
    kept one under it.
  - `pump`, with nothing else: one pump.
  - `advance`, with `delta_ns`, a non-negative integer: the mock clock is
    advanced by that many nanoseconds ([NTST.3.1]).
  - `set`, with `now_ns`, a non-negative integer: the mock clock is set to
    that instant ([NTST.3.1]).
  - `wall_set`, with `utc_ns`, an integer: the wall clock alone is set to
    that instant ([NTST.3.1]).
  - `cache_seed`, with `key`, a string, and `value`, any JSON value, and
    optionally `ttl_ns`, an integer from 0 to 2^63 − 1: `value` is seeded
    under `key` ([NLFC.9.1]), given as [RCTS.1.2.25] gives a `cache_seeds`
    entry's, with `ttl_ns` as the seed's TTL in engine-clock nanoseconds,
    which counts from the engine's first sample ([NLFC.9.4]). An absent
    `ttl_ns`, or `0`, is a seed with no expiry.

  A harness must fail a fixture when the runtime refuses one of its steps
  (a `set` below the current instant, [NTST.3.1]; a `cache_seed` after the
  engine's first stream event, [NLFC.9.2]; an `assert` past a bound), except a refusal the
  fixture pins: a `runtime_error` fixture's ([RCTS.1.2.25]), an `assert`'s
  that carries `refused` ([RCTS.1.2.27]), a pump's under an `adapter`
  kind whose row states the pump's outcome ([RCTS.1.2.10]), a pump's in
  a fixture that carries `expected_pump_statuses` ([RCTS.1.2.30]), and, in a `replay_determinism` fixture that carries
  `tamper`, the step during which the engine halts, which must be the
  fixture's last ([RCTS.1.2.21]).

  A cross-tier fixture's steps take more ([RCTS.1.2.29]). A harness must fail
  a fixture whose array of steps is not an array of objects, and one with a
  step whose `op` names no member of the set, or that lacks a member its op
  requires, carries one it does not take, or gives one a value of another
  type, or gives a slot an object with a `$bytes` or a `$text_bytes` member
  that is not its form above. A deprecated fixture is not run ([RCTS.1.2.12]), so
  its steps are not judged. The set grows only by a change to this clause.
